title: Invertibility of the fixed rational projective-line unit comparisons
statement: Fix distinct primes $\ell,p$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p$, and a separated finite-type $k$-scheme $Y$ as in [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Fix $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ and a finite intermediate extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$. Let $\Lambda=\underline E$ or the finite-subextension-valued $\underline{\overline{\mathbf Q}}_\ell$ of [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] and [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed], with pulled-back coefficients [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Put $P=\mathbf P^1_Y$, $W=P\times_Y P$, $q:P\to Y$, $p_1,p_2:W\to P$, and $\Delta:P\to W$, using [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change]. Write $D(Z)=D(\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_Z})$ for the ordinary unbounded category, with the derived functors of [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull] and tensor of [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom]. Let $\mathcal L_Z=\Loc(\Dbc(Z,\Lambda))$, where $\Dbc$ means bounded cohomology with finite constant local models as in [sk-def-sfb-constructible], and $\Loc$ is the full replete triangulated closure under all small ambient coproducts [sk-def-localizing-closure]. Let $L_Z=\Lambda_Z(1)$ and use the root-normalized shifted comparison $e:p_2^*(L_P[2])\simeq L_W[2]$ of [def-sfb-rational-tate-pullback-comparison]. Let $\beta_M:q^*Rq_*M\to Rp_{2*}p_1^*M$ be the canonical unit--composition--counit exchange of [def-weil-pbc-ambient-ringed-exchange] for the self-cartesian square of $q$, and let $\Pi_{p_2,e,p_1^*M}$ be the fixed twisted projection of [def-sfb-tate-twisted-projection-comparison]. For every $M\in\mathcal L_P$, both $\beta_M$ and $\Pi_{p_2,e,p_1^*M}$ are isomorphisms. Thus the predicate $\mathrm{UnitInversionCondition}(\Lambda,Y,L,e,M)$ of [def-sfb-rational-p1-unit-inversion-condition] holds, for precisely these maps, not for unspecified isomorphisms.

Construction material retained from the earlier split. The following proof-in-words was previously attached to this node. It is preserved here verbatim as source material for the worker who will prove the corresponding Lean declaration; this stage-1 node intentionally has no proof steps.

Former proof step 1:
Apply [lem-sfb-rational-p1-localizing-preservation] to obtain properness, the standing finite-type hypotheses, qcqs, and preservation of every required localizing category. The fixed rational line comparison of [def-sfb-rational-tate-pullback-comparison] is the Cartesian comparison for p_2, with the actual shifted Tate lines; invertibility of ell follows from its nonzero image in k and preservation of units. The two fixed unit maps are the ones named in [def-sfb-rational-p1-unit-inversion-condition].

Former uses: ["lem-sfb-rational-p1-localizing-preservation", "def-sfb-rational-tate-pullback-comparison", "def-sfb-rational-p1-unit-inversion-condition"]
Former elementary flag: False
Former source: {'document': 'literature/blueprint/latest/blueprint/sec-six-functors-basics/sk-prop-p1-adjunction-rational/sk-prop-p1-adjunction-rational-unit-counit.proof.md', 'place': 'Well-definedness (2): identify the fixed maps and their coefficient hypotheses'}

Former proof step 2:
Base change for the final arrow. The cartesian square has $f=q$, $f'=p_2$, $g=q$, $g'=p_1$. Its canonical exchange map $\beta_M:q^*Rq_*M\to Rp_{2*}p_1^*M$ is the unit--pullback-comparison--counit composite of [def-weil-pbc-ambient-ringed-exchange]. To apply the bounded rational theorem with its general ring-object constructibility convention, take any constant-model $M\in\Dbc(P,\Lambda)$. On every stratum its cohomology has a finite constant local model, hence is locally finitely presented over the coefficient ring object by the final inclusion of [det-def-sfb-constructible-local-model]. The same finite stratification therefore witnesses constructibility in [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible], with the same finite cohomological bounds. Consequently $M$ belongs to the bounded category of [det-thm-sfb-proper-base-change-rational], and clause (3) makes its canonical $\beta_M$ an isomorphism. This uses only the inclusion from constant-model constructibility into ring-object constructibility. By [det-def-localizing-closure-ctf-equals-bc] the constant-model $\Dbc$ objects are exactly the $\Dctf$ generators. The extension statement [det-proper-base-change-unbounded-extension] therefore makes this same $\beta_M$ an isomorphism for every $M\in\Loc(\Dbc(P,\Lambda))$. The properness and closure-preservation hypotheses were checked in the preservation lemma. Invert $\beta$ as a natural isomorphism; its direction is $Rp_{2*}p_1^*\to q^*Rq_*$, as required by clause (2).

Former proof step 3:
For $A=p_1^*M$, preservation gives $A\in\mathcal L_W$ and $L_P\in\mathcal L_P$. Apply [det-thm-sf-pf-field-localizing] to $p_2,A,L_P$, with the normalized Cartesian Tate comparison of [def-sfb-rational-tate-pullback-comparison]. Its canonical map, shifted by [2] and conjugated by the tensor-shift isomorphisms, is exactly $\Pi_{p_2,e,A}$ of [def-sfb-tate-twisted-projection-comparison], hence invertible. In particular its inverse has direction $Rp_{2*}(p_1^*M(1)[2])\to (Rp_{2*}p_1^*M)(1)[2]$. Following it by $T_P(\beta_M^{-1})$ has the required target $T_Pq^*Rq_*M$. The finite-coefficient annihilation condition is irrelevant for these rational coefficients.

The characteristic is p, so its prime and inequality facts are exactly the standing facts.

The chosen rational coefficient is admissible: it is literally the finite-extension representative or the finite-subextension-valued algebraic-closure representative. Its termwise exchange is the ambient exchange conjugated by the canonical exact-pullback isomorphisms, so its component is invertible if and only if the ambient component is.
